To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mobility modelling could be applied for handover margins of at least 15 dB, but not for lower handover margins and averaging window values of 10 s or less.

the handover margin should be at least 15 dB, the averaging window should be 15 s, the measurement period should be 1 s, the handover margin and averaging window should be equal, and the channel holding time should be exponentially distributed.

mobility modelling results regarding channel holding time could generally be used, whilst cell residence time results should be used with care, especially when exponential distribution approximations are used, and that a handover margin of 10 dB and averaging window of 15 s are the most appropriate values to use in the handover procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the statistical analysis of handovers and the comparison of these statistics with the predictions of mobility modelling.
the evaluation of handover related parameters and the applicability and accuracy of commonly used assumptions and models in their prediction.
the statistical analysis of the parameters of the handover procedure, and the comparison of the mobility modelling predictions to the statistical analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the handover margin should be set to at least 10 dB, the averaging window to at least 15 s, the measurement period to at least 1 s and the cell residence time to at least 20 s.

the handover margin and the averaging window should be carefully selected, depending on the mobility modelling assumptions and the application, and the channel holding time should be assumed exponentially distributed.
handover statistics are highly dependent on the handover margin and averaging window, and therefore, it is not possible to draw general conclusions regarding the applicability of handover modelling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of the mobility modelling can be used for the estimation of the cell residence time for a wide range of handover margins.
handover related statistics should be used in the design of handover procedures, but mobility modelling results should be used with caution, and only in specific cases.
mobility modelling results could be used to predict cell residence time for a wide range of handover margins, but not the other handover-related parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the handover margin should be chosen carefully in order to achieve the best possible performance.
handover related statistics should not be taken as a given and that their prediction should be done with care.
mobility modelling results could be used to predict the statistics of the handover related parameters for a specific handover procedure, but not for the handover procedure itself.
